name: Barbell Back Squat
doThisNotThat: Sit DOWN between your heels, not back onto a chair: knees travel forward past the toes, torso stays more upright and the quads do the work.
steps: Bar on the upper traps (high bar), hands just outside shoulders, elbows pulled down under the bar.
Unrack, 2 steps back, feet shoulder width, toes out 15-30°.
Big breath into the belly and brace 360° before each rep.
Lower 2-3 s until hip crease is at or below knee; stand up fast.
cues: Spread the floor apart with your feet.
Push your back into the bar on the way up.
Drive the ground away.
homeSwap: Goblet squat with your heaviest DB, 3 s lowering + 1 s pause in the hole, or a 1.5-rep squat (down, half up, down, up).
note: Flat feet: if your knees cave as you stand, film from the front. A slight heel lift (5-10 mm plates under the heels) fixes ankle-limited depth while the Screw cue fixes the cave.
hardestPoint: Just above parallel, where the hip moment arm is longest and most people shoot the hips up first.

name: Front Squat
doThisNotThat: Elbows UP the whole rep. When they drop, the bar rolls forward and your back rounds before your legs fail.
steps: Bar on the front delts touching the throat; clean grip with 2-3 fingers or crossed arms.
Elbows high, parallel to the floor.
Feet shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Sit straight down between the heels, torso near vertical.
cues: Elbows to the ceiling.
Knees out over the pinky toes.
homeSwap: Goblet squat holding the DB vertically against your sternum, elbows inside the knees at the bottom.
note: Your wrists and t-spine are stiff: use straps looped around the bar for the grip until the rack position opens up. The upright torso is the closest squat to a basketball rebound or jump stance.
hardestPoint: Bottom third, where the upper back must stay extended to keep the bar over mid-foot.

name: Goblet Squat
doThisNotThat: Hold the DB tight to the chest and pause 1 s at the bottom. Bouncing out of the hole with the weight drifting away teaches nothing.
steps: Hold one DB vertically by the top head, against your sternum.
Feet just wider than shoulders, toes out 20°.
Lower 3 s; elbows finish inside the knees.
Pause 1 s, then stand fast.
cues: Push your knees out with your elbows.
Stand up through the whole foot.
homeSwap: Already a home move: add a 3 s lowering, a 2 s pause and 1.5 reps once the DB gets light.
note: Best squat for your stiffness: the counterweight lets you sit deep and upright, so the loaded bottom position builds hip and ankle range every set (Afonso 2021: full-range lifting ≈ stretching for ROM).

name: Zercher Squat
doThisNotThat: Keep the bar in the elbow crease and squeeze it to your torso. If it slides to the forearms your back rounds.
steps: Set the bar in a rack at belly height (or deadlift it up).
Hook it in the crooks of both elbows, hands clasped.
Feet shoulder width, brace hard.
Sit down until elbows touch the inside of the thighs, then stand.
cues: Hug the bar into your stomach.
Push the floor away.
homeSwap: Goblet squat with a 2 s pause, DB held horizontally in the elbow crease.
note: Front-loaded and awkward on purpose: it trains the brace and upper-back position you need when someone is hanging on you in a clinch or wrestling tie-up.

name: Box Squat
doThisNotThat: Sit to the box, pause 1 s with tension kept, then explode. Plopping down and rocking off kills the point.
steps: Box set so your hip crease sits at knee height when seated.
Wider stance, toes out, bar on traps.
Sit back and down under control until you touch.
Pause 1 s without relaxing, stand explosively.
cues: Touch the box like it is made of glass.
Jump the bar up.
homeSwap: Goblet box squat to a chair: 1 s pause, then stand as fast as possible.
note: The pause kills the stretch reflex, so you learn to produce force from a dead stop: starting strength for your first step off the line in football or sprinting.

name: Pause Squat
doThisNotThat: Pause in the bottom with your brace locked and still. Use about 80-85% of your normal squat weight.
steps: Normal back squat setup.
Lower 2-3 s to depth.
Hold 2 s at the bottom without bouncing or relaxing.
Drive up fast.
cues: Stay tight like a spring.
Drive the floor away.
homeSwap: Goblet pause squat, 3 s hold in the hole.
note: The hold at the bottom is loaded mobility for your stiff hips and ankles: your nervous system learns the deep position is safe, so it gives you more range.

name: Heels-Elevated Squat
doThisNotThat: Narrow stance, heels on a 2-5 cm wedge, knees drive way past the toes. It is a quad builder, not a hip squat.
steps: Heels on a slant board or 2 plates, feet close (hip width or less).
DB goblet or DBs at your sides, torso upright.
Lower 3 s, knees forward over the toes until hamstrings touch calves.
Stand without letting the knees cave.
cues: Push your knees over your toes.
Keep your chest tall to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Already home-friendly: stand on books, DBs at sides, 3 s lowering.
note: Works around stiff ankles so you get full knee bend; the deep knee flexion is where the quads get the most stretch (lengthened bias).

name: Safety Bar Squat
doThisNotThat: Hold the handles low and push your upper back into the pad. The bar wants to fold you forward.
steps: Pad on the traps, handles in front.
Feet shoulder width.
Lower 2-3 s to depth.
Stand while pushing the upper back up into the bar.
cues: Push your head back into the bar.
Spread the floor.
homeSwap: Goblet squat with your heaviest DB, 3 s lowering + 1 s pause in the hole, or a 1.5-rep squat (down, half up, down, up).
note: Easier on stiff shoulders than a straight bar, so you can squat heavy without forcing a back-rack position you do not have yet.

name: Smith Machine Squat
doThisNotThat: Put the feet slightly forward of the bar so you can sit straight down; feet right under the bar loads the knees awkwardly.
steps: Bar on traps, feet 10-20 cm in front of the bar line.
Unrack by twisting the bar, set the safeties at just below depth.
Lower 3 s to depth.
Stand fast.
cues: Push the floor away.
Stay tall against the bar.
homeSwap: Goblet squat with your heaviest DB, 3 s lowering + 1 s pause in the hole, or a 1.5-rep squat (down, half up, down, up).
note: Fixed bar path removes balance demands: good for quad size, poor for athletic transfer. Pair it with a free single-leg move.

name: Hack Squat
doThisNotThat: Feet low and narrow on the platform, go DEEP. High, wide feet turn it into a weak glute press.
steps: Back flat on the pad, shoulders under the pads.
Feet hip width, lower-middle of the platform.
Release handles, lower 3 s until hips are below knees.
Drive up to just short of lockout.
cues: Push the platform through the floor.
Knees track over your middle toes.
homeSwap: Sissy squat holding a door frame, or a heels-elevated goblet squat on 2 plates/books, knees driving far past toes.
note: The deep position stretches the quads hardest; stop each set 1 rep short of failure, then add 3-5 lengthened partials in the bottom half.

name: Belt Squat
doThisNotThat: Hold the handles lightly and stay upright. The point is loading the legs with zero spine load.
steps: Belt around the hips, chain centered under you.
Feet shoulder width on the platforms.
Squat straight down to depth.
Stand up without rocking forward.
cues: Drive the floor down.
Hips straight up the chain.
homeSwap: Goblet squat on two chairs holding a DB hanging between your legs (dead-hang DB squat).
note: No bar on the back: lets you train legs hard the day after sparring when your neck and back are beat.

name: Pendulum Squat
doThisNotThat: Full depth, slow lowering. The machine curve makes the bottom the hardest part, so do not shortchange it.
steps: Back on the pad, shoulders under the pads.
Feet mid-platform, hip width.
Lower 3 s to full depth.
Drive up to near lockout.
cues: Push through the whole foot.
Knees forward.
homeSwap: Sissy squat holding a door frame, or a heels-elevated goblet squat on 2 plates/books, knees driving far past toes.
note: Loads the quads most where they are longest; finish the last set with bottom-half partials.

name: V-Squat
doThisNotThat: Full range and a soft lockout. Half reps with heavy plates do little.
steps: Shoulders under pads, back on the pad.
Feet shoulder width on the plate.
Lower 3 s to full depth.
Stand to just short of lockout.
cues: Drive the plate away.
homeSwap: Goblet squat with your heaviest DB, 3 s lowering + 1 s pause in the hole, or a 1.5-rep squat (down, half up, down, up).
note: Machine stability lets you push close to failure safely on quads, which a heavy free-weight squat does not (1 RIR there).

name: Sissy Squat
doThisNotThat: Hips stay extended and knees travel far forward. If you sit back it becomes a normal squat and loses the quad stretch.
steps: Hold a door frame or post with one hand.
Rise onto the balls of your feet.
Lean back while knees drive forward and down, body a straight line from knees to shoulders.
Go as deep as you control, then pull back up with the quads.
cues: Push your knees toward the wall in front.
Keep hips and shoulders in one line.
homeSwap: Already a home move; hold a DB to the chest once 15 reps is easy.
note: Trains the rectus femoris at long length (hip extended + knee bent), the head most squats miss. Start shallow: knees get sore fast.

name: Leg Press
doThisNotThat: Lower until your knees nearly touch your chest with your low back still on the pad. Heavy quarter reps are an ego lift.
steps: Back and hips flat on the pad, seat at a comfortable depth.
Feet mid-platform, shoulder width, toes slightly out.
Release safeties, lower 3 s as deep as the low back stays down.
Press to just short of locked knees.
cues: Push the sled through the wall.
Knees out over your toes.
homeSwap: Goblet squat with your heaviest DB, 3 s lowering + 1 s pause in the hole, or a 1.5-rep squat (down, half up, down, up).
note: Your flat feet still matter here: press through big-toe ball and heel (tripod) so the knees do not drift inward at the bottom.

name: Single-Leg Leg Press
doThisNotThat: Use about 40% of your two-leg weight and go deep. Too heavy and the hip shifts and the low back peels off.
steps: Seat back, one foot centered on the platform.
Other foot on the floor or frame.
Lower 3 s until knee approaches chest, hips stay down.
Press up without twisting.
cues: Push through the middle of your foot.
Knee tracks over the second toe.
homeSwap: Rear-foot-elevated split squat on a couch or step, DBs at your sides, 3 s lowering.
note: Exposes left-right differences that your bilateral numbers hide; start with the weaker leg and match reps.

name: Leg Press (High Foot)
doThisNotThat: High feet move the work to glutes and adductors. Go deep enough that the hips flex hard, low back staying down.
steps: Feet high on the platform, slightly wider than shoulders.
Lower 3 s until thighs approach the torso.
Press through the heels to just short of lockout.
cues: Drive through your heels.
Push the platform up and away.
homeSwap: Single-leg hip thrust with shoulders on the couch, DB on the hip, 2 s squeeze at the top.
note: Good on days your knees are sore: high placement reduces knee bend for the same depth.

name: Leg Press (Low Foot)
doThisNotThat: Low and narrow feet bias the quads. Let your heels stay down while knees travel well past the toes.
steps: Feet low on the platform, hip width.
Lower 3 s, knees forward.
Press to just short of lockout.
cues: Push with the whole foot.
Knees over toes.
homeSwap: Sissy squat holding a door frame, or a heels-elevated goblet squat on 2 plates/books, knees driving far past toes.
note: Your ankles are stiff, so the heels may lift: go only as deep as the heel stays down, and move up 2 cm if it pops.

name: Bodyweight Squat
doThisNotThat: Pause 1 s at the bottom and stand fast. Bodyweight squats are a mobility and speed drill, not a strength builder past 20 reps.
steps: Feet shoulder width, toes out 15-20°.
Arms forward for counterbalance.
Lower 2 s to full depth.
Pause, then stand explosively.
cues: Spread the floor.
Reach your arms to the wall.
homeSwap: Already home; add a jump at the top (squat jump) for power.
note: Use it in warm-ups to groove the Screw cue: feel the arch rise and knees line up before you ever load it.

name: Conventional Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Pull the slack out of the bar before it leaves the floor. Jerking it up rounds your back and wastes the leg drive.
steps: Mid-foot under the bar, feet hip width.
Hinge and grip just outside the legs.
Shins to the bar, chest up, lats tight ("protect your armpits").
Pull the slack out until the bar clicks, then push the floor away.
Lock out with glutes, not by leaning back.
cues: Push the floor away.
Drag the bar up your legs.
Bend the bar around your shins.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: Stop sets when a rep visibly slows (Pareja-Blanco 2017 logic): grinding deadlifts costs more recovery than any other lift and dulls your sprint and jump work for days.
hardestPoint: Off the floor to just below the knee, where the hip moment arm is longest.

name: Sumo Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Spread the floor with your feet and push the knees out over the toes before pulling. Without that, it is a bad conventional pull.
steps: Stance wide, shins near the plates, toes out 30-45°.
Grip inside the knees, arms vertical.
Hips down, chest up, knees forced out.
Push the floor apart and stand up.
cues: Spread the floor.
Push your knees to the plates.
homeSwap: Sumo goblet squat with a DB hanging between your feet, pause at the bottom.
note: Your stiff hips may not allow a deep sumo yet: start with a stance only slightly wider than conventional and widen as the adductors loosen.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Stand in the center and push the floor away like a jump. It is the best heavy lift for athletes because the load sits in line with your center of mass.
steps: Step into the middle, feet hip width.
Hips down, grip the handles centered.
Chest up, lats tight.
Push the floor away fast and stand tall.
cues: Jump the floor away (without leaving it).
Stand tall through the crown.
homeSwap: DB suitcase deadlift: one DB in each hand at your sides, same push-the-floor pattern.
note: High-handle trap bar pulls are a great power exercise: light-to-moderate loads lifted as fast as possible transfer to vertical jump.

name: Deficit Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Only 2-5 cm of deficit, and only if you can keep a flat back from the deeper start.
steps: Stand on a 2-5 cm plate.
Normal deadlift setup, hips a bit lower.
Push the floor away, keep the bar close.
cues: Push the floor away.
Keep the bar against your shins.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: Your stiff hamstrings may round your back in the deficit; skip this until a normal deadlift from the floor is clean.

name: Snatch-Grip Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Wide grip means deeper start and more upper-back work. Use 70-80% of your normal deadlift.
steps: Grip wide (index fingers near the rings or wider).
Hips lower, chest up.
Push the floor away, keep the bar close.
cues: Bend the bar around you.
Push the floor away.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: Builds the thick upper back that holds posture under fatigue in boxing and wrestling.

name: Romanian Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Push your hips BACK until the hamstrings stop you, keeping a soft knee. Bending the knees more to get the bar lower turns it into a sloppy deadlift.
steps: Start standing, bar at the hips, double overhand grip.
Soft knees (about 15-20°), fixed.
Push hips back, bar slides down the thighs 3 s.
Stop when hips stop moving back (usually mid-shin).
Drive hips forward to stand.
cues: Push your hips to the wall behind you.
Drag the bar down your legs.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: The loaded stretch on stiff hamstrings is your mobility work: full-range lifting improves ROM about as much as stretching (Afonso 2021).

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Let the DBs slide down the front of your thighs. Letting them swing forward of the knees loads your low back instead of the hamstrings.
steps: DBs at your thighs, palms in.
Soft knees, fixed.
Hips back 3 s, DBs down the legs.
Stop when hips stop moving back, stand.
cues: Hips to the wall behind you.
Keep the DBs touching your legs.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: Light home DBs: add a 2 s pause at the bottom stretch and slow the lowering to 4 s to make them heavy.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Hips stay square to the floor. Opening the hip toward the ceiling feels deeper but loses the glute.
steps: DB in the hand opposite the standing leg.
Soft standing knee, tripod foot.
Hinge as the back leg reaches back, body like a seesaw.
Stop when hips want to rotate open, return.
cues: Reach your back heel to the wall.
Point both hip bones at the floor.
homeSwap: Already home; hold the DB in the same-side hand to make balance harder.
note: Single-leg balance under load is exactly where your flat foot collapses: grip with the tripod foot and do the Screw on the standing foot every rep.

name: B-Stance Romanian Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Front leg does ~80% of the work, back toe only for balance. If you push off the back foot it is just an RDL.
steps: Working foot flat, back foot toes beside the working heel.
DBs at thighs.
Hinge back 3 s on the front leg.
Stand by driving the front hip forward.
cues: Push your front heel into the floor.
Hips to the wall.
homeSwap: Already home; DBs in both hands, 3 s lowering.
note: A bridge to single-leg RDLs when your balance is the limiter: you can load it heavier while still training one side at a time.

name: Cable Romanian Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Stand far enough back that the cable pulls you down and back at the bottom; that keeps tension in the stretch.
steps: Low pulley, straight bar or rope.
Step back 1-2 steps, soft knees.
Hinge 3 s until hamstrings stop you.
Drive the hips through to stand.
cues: Hips to the wall behind you.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: Constant tension at the bottom: useful as a lighter, higher-rep hamstring finisher.

name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Each rep starts from the floor with near-straight knees, light weight only. Rounding to reach the floor defeats it.
steps: Bar on the floor, feet hip width.
Knees barely bent.
Hinge to grip with a flat back.
Stand by driving hips forward, lower with control.
cues: Push your hips back.
Keep the bar against your legs.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: Your hamstrings are stiff: if you cannot reach the bar with a flat back, elevate it on plates and keep the RDL instead.

name: Good Morning
doThisNotThat: Use light weight and hinge only as far as your back stays flat. The long lever makes small loads heavy.
steps: Bar on the traps like a squat.
Soft knees.
Push hips back 3 s, torso toward parallel.
Drive hips forward to stand.
cues: Hips to the wall.
Keep the bar pinned to your back.
homeSwap: DB good morning holding one DB at your chest, or bodyweight hands-behind-head with 4 s lowering.
note: Trains the hip hinge you need for a stable boxing stance and sprawl; keep it light (RIR 2-3).

name: Rack Pull
doThisNotThat: Set the bar just below the knee and lock out with the glutes. Leaning back at the top is not a lockout.
steps: Bar on pins just below or at the knee.
Grip, lats tight, chest up.
Push the hips forward to stand tall.
Lower back to the pins under control.
cues: Hips through.
Stand tall.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: Builds the upper back and grip without the full-range fatigue. Not a substitute for a full hinge for hamstring growth.

name: Back Extension
doThisNotThat: Hinge at the hips, not the spine. Pad just below the hip crease so you can fold over it.
steps: Set the pad just below the hip bones.
Feet locked, body straight.
Hinge down 3 s until hamstrings stop you.
Drive hips into the pad to come up to a straight line, not past it.
cues: Push your hips into the pad.
Reach your chest to the wall.
homeSwap: Single-leg hip hinge to the floor or a prone hip extension off the edge of the bed.
note: Rounding the upper back slightly and squeezing the glutes makes it a glute builder; staying flat makes it a hamstring builder.

name: Reverse Hyperextension
doThisNotThat: Swing the legs up with the glutes to a straight line, not higher. Overextending the low back is the mistake.
steps: Lie face down, hips at the edge of the pad.
Grip the handles.
Lift the legs to body height with straight knees.
Lower 2 s with control.
cues: Kick your heels to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Lie face down on a bed or bench, hips at the edge, lift straight legs to body height.
note: Decompresses the spine while working the glutes; handy after heavy squats or a day of sparring.

name: Forward Lunge
doThisNotThat: Step out and push back in one move, landing heel-toe. Stepping too short drives the knee forward and pinches it.
steps: DBs at your sides, feet hip width.
Step forward about 2-3 foot lengths.
Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Push hard off the front foot to return.
cues: Push the floor back to return.
Land quiet.
homeSwap: Already home; hold DBs and add a 1 s pause at the bottom.
note: The deceleration on landing is what basketball and tennis demand on every hard stop. Stick the landing on your tripod foot.

name: Reverse Lunge
doThisNotThat: Step back and keep about 80% of your weight on the front foot. Pushing off the back foot steals the work.
steps: DBs at your sides.
Step back 2-3 foot lengths.
Lower straight down, slight forward torso lean.
Drive through the front foot to stand.
cues: Push the front foot through the floor.
Back knee straight down.
homeSwap: Already home; hold DBs and do 3 s lowering.
note: Kinder to the knees than forward lunges. A slight torso lean shifts the work toward the glute.

name: Walking Lunge
doThisNotThat: Long steps, back knee nearly kisses the floor, and no pause at the top. The continuous flow is the point.
steps: DBs at your sides.
Step forward long, lower the back knee near the floor.
Drive through the front foot straight into the next step.
cues: Push the floor behind you.
Stay tall.
homeSwap: Walking lunge with DBs in a hallway, or reverse lunge in place.
note: One of the best home leg moves with light DBs because 20+ steps make even light weight hard.

name: Lateral Lunge
doThisNotThat: Sit back into the bent hip with the other leg straight and foot flat. Staying upright just stretches the adductor without load.
steps: Wide stance, toes forward.
Shift into one hip, sitting back.
Other leg straight, both feet flat.
Push back to center.
cues: Push the floor sideways to return.
Sit your hips back.
homeSwap: Already home; hold a DB as a goblet.
note: Lateral force for every cut and shuffle in basketball, tennis and pickleball, and it loads your stiff adductors at length.

name: Curtsy Lunge
doThisNotThat: Step behind and across but keep the front knee tracking over the toes; letting it collapse inward defeats the purpose.
steps: Stand tall, DBs at sides or goblet.
Step one leg behind and across.
Lower until front thigh is near parallel.
Drive back up through the front foot.
cues: Push the front knee out over the little toe.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Directly challenges the knee-cave part of your flat-foot cascade; use the Screw cue on the front foot.

name: Deficit Reverse Lunge
doThisNotThat: Stand on a 5-10 cm step and step back down. The extra depth is a deep glute and quad stretch, so go slow.
steps: Stand on a step or plate, DBs at your sides.
Step back off the platform.
Lower until front hip is below knee.
Drive back up onto the step.
cues: Push the step away.
homeSwap: Already home: use a stair.
note: Lengthened bias for glutes with light DBs, which makes it one of the best home glute builders.

name: Split Squat
doThisNotThat: Feet stay planted, straight up and down. Bouncing the back foot or shifting forward turns it into a lunge.
steps: Long split stance, back heel up.
DBs at sides.
Drop the back knee straight down 3 s.
Drive up through the front foot.
cues: Elevator straight down.
Push the front foot through the floor.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Good starting point before Bulgarians: the back foot on the floor gives you more balance help.

name: Dumbbell Bulgarian Split Squat
aliases: rear foot elevated split squat dumbbell
doThisNotThat: Set the front foot so the knee can travel forward and the back knee drops straight. A too-long stance turns it into a hip flexor stretch.
steps: Back foot laces-down on a bench at knee height.
Front foot ~2 foot lengths ahead.
DBs at your sides.
Lower 3 s until the back knee nearly touches the floor.
Drive up through the front foot.
cues: Push the front foot through the floor.
Back knee straight to the floor.
homeSwap: Already home: couch for the back foot.
note: Best home quad and glute builder with light DBs: single-leg doubles the relative load. Slight forward lean = more glute.

name: Barbell Bulgarian Split Squat
doThisNotThat: Start lighter than you think. Balance with a bar on your back is harder; if you wobble, go back to DBs.
steps: Bar on traps.
Back foot on bench, front foot 2 lengths ahead.
Lower 3 s.
Drive up.
cues: Push the floor away.
Stay tall.
homeSwap: Rear-foot-elevated split squat on a couch or step, DBs at your sides, 3 s lowering.
note: Only use it once DB BSS needs DBs heavier than you can hold.

name: Front-Foot Elevated Split Squat
doThisNotThat: Front foot on a 5-10 cm plate lets you go deeper than the floor. Use that depth slowly.
steps: Front foot on a plate or step.
Back foot on the floor, heel up.
Lower 3 s until the back knee touches the floor.
Drive up.
cues: Push the front foot down.
homeSwap: Already home: front foot on a book or stair.
note: Extra depth stretches the front glute and the back-leg hip flexor at once; great for your stiff hips.

name: Step-Up
doThisNotThat: Drive through the top foot only. Pushing off the bottom foot makes it easy and useless.
steps: Box at knee height or a bit lower.
Whole foot on the box, DBs at sides.
Lean slightly forward, stand up using the top leg.
Lower 3 s back down.
cues: Push the box down.
Stand tall on top.
homeSwap: Already home: a stair or chair.
note: Lower slowly: the eccentric on a step-up is the knee-protecting part for landing from jumps.

name: Lateral Step-Up
doThisNotThat: Stand side-on and keep the working knee over the second toe. The inside knee collapse is what you are training out.
steps: Stand beside a box with one foot on top.
Push through the top foot to stand.
Lower the other foot to tap the floor slowly.
cues: Push the box down.
Knee over the little toe.
homeSwap: Already home: stair, side-on.
note: Directly fights the knee-cave part of your flat-foot cascade.

name: Skater Squat
doThisNotThat: Back knee touches a pad behind you; arms reach forward for balance. Diving forward to cheat depth misses the quads.
steps: Stand on one leg, other knee bent behind you.
Arms forward.
Lower until the back knee touches a pad or folded towel.
Stand up through the front foot.
cues: Reach your arms to the wall.
Knee lightly to the pad.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Great single-leg strength test: your goal is 5 clean reps each leg with no hand assist.

name: Pistol Squat
doThisNotThat: Hold a light DB forward as a counterweight. It makes depth easier and teaches control.
steps: Stand on one leg, other leg forward.
Arms or a light DB out front.
Sit down slowly as low as you control.
Stand up without bouncing.
cues: Reach forward.
Push the floor away.
homeSwap: Already home: start with pistols to a chair.
note: Your stiff ankles will limit depth: put the heel on a book until dorsiflexion improves.

name: Cossack Squat
doThisNotThat: The straight leg toes point up and the squatting heel stays down. Go only as deep as your heel stays flat.
steps: Very wide stance.
Shift to one side and sit down, other leg straight, toes up.
Counterweight DB held in front.
Push back to center and switch.
cues: Sit into your hip.
Heel heavy.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Loaded mobility for your stiff adductors and ankles: one of the best for the lateral range needed in wrestling and tennis.

name: Lying Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Press your hips into the pad so they do not rise, and lower slowly. Hips popping up shortens the hamstrings and kills the stretch.
steps: Kneecaps just off the end of the pad, ankle pad just above the heels.
Hips pressed down, grip the handles.
Curl to full flexion.
Lower 3 s to full extension.
cues: Pull your heels to your glutes.
Push your hips through the pad.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: Seated leg curls grew hamstrings more than lying ones (Maeo 2021) because the hip is flexed and the hamstrings are longer. If both are available, prefer seated.

name: Seated Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Lean your torso forward against the thigh pad. More hip flexion = more hamstring stretch = more growth.
steps: Knees lined up with the machine pivot.
Thigh pad locked down tight.
Lean the torso forward.
Curl to full flexion, lower 3 s.
cues: Pull your heels under the seat.
Lean your chest toward your knees.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: Seated leg curls grew the hamstrings more than lying leg curls in Maeo 2021, due to the long hamstring position. Last set: lengthened partials in the top half.

name: Standing Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Keep the hips square and still; rotating to finish the curl uses your back.
steps: Thigh against the pad, ankle pad above the heel.
Hips square, hold the handles.
Curl fully, lower 3 s.
cues: Pull your heel to your butt.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: Each leg separate: shows imbalances common in sprinters. Match reps on both sides.

name: Single-Leg Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Same machine, one leg at a time, lower slower than you lift.
steps: Same setup as the two-leg curl.
One leg in.
Curl fully, lower 3-4 s.
cues: Pull the heel in.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: One leg at a time lets you lower a weight you can only lift with two legs (two-up, one-down eccentric overload).

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
doThisNotThat: Fight the fall the whole way with hips straight. Breaking at the hips makes it easier and less protective.
steps: Kneel on a pad, ankles anchored under a couch or held by a partner.
Body straight from knees to head, glutes tight.
Lower as slowly as possible.
Catch yourself with your hands, push back up.
cues: Keep a straight line from knees to head.
Fall as slowly as you can.
homeSwap: Already home: anchor feet under the couch.
note: Programs including Nordics reduced hamstring injuries by up to about 51% (van Dyk 2019; a later reappraisal is less certain). 2 × 4-6, 1-2x a week is enough.

name: Slider Hamstring Curl
doThisNotThat: Keep the hips up the whole set. Hips dropping turns it into a sloppy bridge.
steps: Lie on your back, heels on sliders or a towel on a smooth floor.
Bridge your hips up.
Slide heels out slowly 3 s, hips stay up.
Pull heels back to your glutes.
cues: Pull your heels to your glutes.
Push your hips to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Already home: socks on a hard floor.
note: Best home hamstring curl. Make it single-leg once 12 two-leg reps is easy.

name: Stability Ball Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Hips stay up as the ball rolls in. Hips sagging puts it all on the back.
steps: Lie on your back, heels on the ball.
Bridge up.
Curl the ball in, hips high.
Roll out 3 s.
cues: Pull the ball to your butt.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: The unstable ball also trains the small ankle muscles your flat feet need.

name: Glute-Ham Raise
doThisNotThat: Knees just behind the pad; lower to horizontal under control and curl up using the hamstrings, not by hinging.
steps: Feet on the plate, knees just behind the pad.
Body straight.
Lower to horizontal.
Curl back up with hamstrings.
cues: Pull yourself up with your heels.
Straight line from knees to head.
homeSwap: Nordic hamstring curl with feet under a couch.
note: Trains hamstrings at both the knee and hip, like they work in a sprint.

name: Leg Extension
doThisNotThat: Lean back slightly or recline the seat. A more open hip lengthens the rectus femoris and makes the quads work harder.
steps: Knee joint lined up with the machine pivot.
Ankle pad just above the ankle.
Grip the handles, lean back slightly.
Extend to straight, lower 3 s to full bend.
cues: Kick the pad to the ceiling.
Lower slowly under control.
homeSwap: Sissy squat holding a door frame, or a heels-elevated goblet squat on 2 plates/books, knees driving far past toes.
note: Reclining lengthens the rectus femoris (it crosses the hip), which should load it harder; that is mechanism-based. Last set: lengthened partials in the bottom half.

name: Single-Leg Leg Extension
doThisNotThat: One leg at a time to fix imbalances; same slow lowering.
steps: Same setup as the two-leg extension.
One leg.
Extend fully, lower 3 s.
cues: Kick the pad up.
homeSwap: Sissy squat holding a door frame, or a heels-elevated goblet squat on 2 plates/books, knees driving far past toes.
note: Quads are often weaker on the side that collapses most (often the flatter foot); start with that leg.

name: Reverse Nordic
doThisNotThat: Hips stay extended and body straight from knees to head as you lean back. Bending at the hips removes the stretch.
steps: Kneel on a pad, toes tucked or flat.
Squeeze glutes, body straight.
Lean back slowly as far as you control.
Pull back up with the quads.
cues: Straight line from knees to head.
Lean back slowly.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Loads the quads and hip flexors at length; great for your stiff hip flexors and knee health in deceleration.

name: Spanish Squat
doThisNotThat: Sit back into the band with shins vertical and hold. It loads the quads with little knee shear.
steps: Loop a heavy band around a post and behind both knees.
Step back until the band is tight.
Sit down with vertical shins, torso upright.
Hold 30-45 s.
cues: Push your knees back into the band.
homeSwap: Wall sit at about 70-90° knee bend, 30-45 s holds.
note: Isometric holds can calm down patellar tendon pain; useful after lots of jumping. Five 45 s holds is a common dose (grade C).

name: Terminal Knee Extension
doThisNotThat: Lock the knee fully against the band. Most of the benefit is in the last 10-20°.
steps: Band around the back of the knee, anchored in front.
Step back until tight.
Let the knee bend 20-30°.
Straighten fully and squeeze 1 s.
cues: Push the back of your knee into the band.
homeSwap: Single-leg wall sit or straight-leg raise, 1 s squeeze at the top.
note: Rehab and warm-up tool. Pair with the Screw cue to line up knee and foot before squats.

name: Wall Sit
doThisNotThat: Thighs parallel, shins vertical, push through the heels. Hands off the thighs.
steps: Back against a wall.
Slide down until thighs are parallel.
Shins vertical, feet flat.
Hold.
cues: Push the wall up with your back.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Isometric holds are a good knee-friendly way to train quads the day before a game.

name: Standing Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Pause 2 s in the deepest stretch at the bottom. Bouncing out of it uses the tendon, not the muscle.
steps: Balls of the feet on the edge of the step.
Knees straight but not locked.
Lower 2 s to the deepest stretch, pause 2 s.
Rise as high as possible, squeeze 1 s.
cues: Push the platform through the floor.
Rise tall onto your big toe.
homeSwap: Single-leg calf raise off a stair, holding a DB, 2 s pause at the bottom stretch.
note: Lengthened partials (bottom half only) grew the calves more than full reps (Kassiano 2023). Finish every set with them.

name: Seated Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Same deep 2 s stretch at the bottom. The bent knee shifts work to the soleus.
steps: Knees under the pad, balls of feet on the edge.
Lower 2 s to full stretch, pause.
Rise high, squeeze.
cues: Push the pad up with your toes.
homeSwap: Seated on a chair, heavy DB on each knee, balls of feet on a book.
note: The soleus is the main calf muscle for running; strong soleus = more running economy for XC.

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Keep the knees straight and safety stops on. Let the platform travel all the way into the stretch.
steps: Balls of feet on the bottom edge of the platform.
Knees straight, safeties engaged.
Lower to full stretch, pause 2 s.
Push up high.
cues: Push the platform with your big toes.
homeSwap: Single-leg calf raise off a stair, holding a DB, 2 s pause at the bottom stretch.
note: Easy to load heavy with zero balance demand; finish with lengthened partials.

name: Donkey Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Hips flexed so the gastrocs are already stretched; go to the deepest stretch and pause.
steps: Hinge forward, hands on a bench.
Balls of feet on a step.
Lower deep, pause 2 s.
Rise high.
cues: Rise onto your big toes.
homeSwap: Single-leg calf raise off a stair, holding a DB, 2 s pause at the bottom stretch.
note: The hip flexion lengthens the gastrocnemius further, a cheap lengthened-bias calf builder.

name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Rise over the big toe, not rolling out to the little toe. That is your flat foot leaking force sideways.
steps: Stand on one foot on a step, hold a wall.
DB in the same-side hand.
Lower 2 s to the deepest stretch, pause.
Rise high over the big toe.
cues: Push the step down with your big toe.
homeSwap: Already home: stair + DB.
note: Strengthens the arch-supporting muscles (the tibialis posterior works hard here); the best calf and foot exercise for your flat feet.

name: Tibialis Raise
doThisNotThat: Lean your back against a wall with heels forward; the further out the feet, the harder.
steps: Back against a wall, heels 30-60 cm out.
Legs straight.
Pull your toes up to your shins as high as possible.
Lower slowly.
cues: Pull your toes to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Balances calf work and protects the shins from running load (shin splints are common in XC). Grade C.

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
doThisNotThat: Chin tucked and ribs down at the top. Arching the low back to "finish" moves the work out of the glutes.
steps: Shoulder blades on a bench edge, bar padded over the hips.
Feet flat, shins vertical at the top.
Lower hips 2 s.
Drive up until hips are level with knees, squeeze 1 s.
cues: Push your knees forward.
Drive the bar to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Single-leg hip thrust with shoulders on the couch, DB on the hip, 2 s squeeze at the top.
note: The thrust loads the glutes hardest at full hip extension, the opposite of a squat; doing both covers the whole range. At home, go single-leg to make light DBs hard.

name: Dumbbell Hip Thrust
doThisNotThat: Hold the DB on the hip crease with both hands; pause 2 s at the top.
steps: Upper back on a couch or bench.
DB on the hips.
Lower 2 s, drive up, squeeze 2 s.
cues: Push your knees forward.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: With light DBs, pause at the top and go single-leg to make it hard.

name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
doThisNotThat: Keep the hips level. One side dropping means the working glute is losing.
steps: Upper back on a bench, one foot planted.
Other knee pulled up.
Lower 2 s, drive up, squeeze.
cues: Push through your heel.
Keep the belt line level.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Single-leg hip extension is how you sprint and push off; this is the most sport-specific glute builder at home.

name: Hip Thrust Machine
doThisNotThat: Same chin-tucked, ribs-down finish. Machines make it easy to overextend the back.
steps: Back on the pad, belt over the hips.
Feet so shins are vertical at the top.
Drive up, squeeze 1 s, lower 2 s.
cues: Push the belt to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Single-leg hip thrust with shoulders on the couch, DB on the hip, 2 s squeeze at the top.
note: Simple to push close to failure safely: good for the last set of a glute day.

name: Glute Bridge
doThisNotThat: Squeeze the glutes for 2 s at the top with ribs down; fast bounce reps barely work.
steps: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat.
Push through heels, lift hips.
Squeeze 2 s, lower slowly.
cues: Push the floor away with your heels.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Good warm-up to wake the glutes before sprinting; your arm-first sequencing starts with lazy hips.

name: Single-Leg Glute Bridge
doThisNotThat: Hips level; pause at the top.
steps: On your back, one foot planted, other leg straight up or knee hugged.
Lift hips.
Squeeze 2 s, lower slowly.
cues: Push the floor away with your heel.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Hugging the other knee to the chest stops you from arching the back to cheat.

name: Frog Pump
doThisNotThat: Soles together, knees out, short fast reps with a hard squeeze. It is a pump finisher, not a strength move.
steps: On your back, soles of feet together, knees out.
Heels close to your butt.
Thrust hips up, squeeze.
Repeat fast.
cues: Push your knees to the floor.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: A quick finisher: 2 × 20-30 for a glute pump without fatiguing your legs before sport.

name: Cable Glute Kickback
doThisNotThat: Hinge forward ~45° and kick back and up with a slight bend in the knee. Swinging the leg uses momentum and your back.
steps: Ankle cuff on, low pulley.
Hold the frame, hinge forward 30-45°.
Kick back until the hip is fully extended.
Return slowly.
cues: Kick your heel to the wall behind you.
homeSwap: Quadruped donkey kick with a DB behind the knee.
note: The hinge puts the glute in a longer position at the start, giving more stretch.

name: Glute Kickback Machine
doThisNotThat: Full range and a 1 s squeeze at the top; no low-back arch.
steps: Chest on the pad, foot on the plate.
Kick back to full hip extension.
Squeeze, return slowly.
cues: Push the plate to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Quadruped donkey kick with a DB behind the knee.
note: Good pump finisher after squats or lunges.

name: Hip Abduction Machine
doThisNotThat: Lean your torso forward slightly. It shifts the work to the upper glute, which is the knee-cave fixer.
steps: Sit with knees on the pads.
Lean forward 20-30°.
Push the pads out as far as possible.
Return slowly.
cues: Push the pads to the walls.
homeSwap: Side-lying hip abduction, toes slightly down, 2 s pause at the top.
note: The glute med stops the knee caving inward when your arch collapses; this is the gym version of the Screw cue.

name: Cable Hip Abduction
doThisNotThat: Stand tall and lift the leg out to the side without leaning. Leaning means the weight is too heavy.
steps: Cuff on the outside ankle, low pulley.
Stand side-on, hold the frame.
Lift the leg out 30-45°.
Return slowly.
cues: Push your heel to the wall.
homeSwap: Side-lying hip abduction.
note: The standing leg works too: grip the tripod foot to keep the arch up.

name: Banded Lateral Walk
doThisNotThat: Stay low in a quarter squat and keep tension the whole time; feet never come together.
steps: Band above the knees or around the ankles.
Quarter squat, feet hip width.
Step sideways 10-15 steps each way.
cues: Push your knees out against the band.
homeSwap: Side-lying hip abduction, or lateral shuffles in a quarter squat.
note: Pre-game activation for cutting sports: wakes up the glute med before you change direction.

name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
doThisNotThat: Keep the top leg slightly behind you with toes pointing down. Bringing it forward turns it into a hip flexor move.
steps: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent.
Top leg straight, slightly behind the body, toes down.
Lift 30-40 cm.
Pause 1 s, lower slowly.
cues: Push your heel to the wall.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Simple and effective for the knee-cave part of the flat-foot cascade.

name: Copenhagen Plank
doThisNotThat: Start with the bench at the knee (short lever) and work toward the ankle. Jumping straight to the long lever is how groins get tweaked.
steps: Side plank with your top leg on a bench (knee for short lever, ankle for long).
Bottom leg under the bench.
Lift the hips into a straight line.
Hold or do slow reps lifting the bottom leg to the bench.
cues: Push the bench down with your top leg.
homeSwap: Already home: use a couch.
note: One Copenhagen exercise 3x/week preseason then 1x/week was linked to 41% lower odds of groin problems (Harøy 2019).

name: Adduction Machine
doThisNotThat: Set the start as wide as is comfortable and lower slowly. The wide, stretched position is where the growth is.
steps: Sit, knees on the pads, start wide.
Squeeze the pads together.
Return 3 s to the widest position.
cues: Squeeze the pads together.
homeSwap: Copenhagen plank, or lying adduction with a DB-free side plank.
note: Your adductors are stiff: the wide loaded stretch here improves your squat depth and lateral range.

name: Cable Hip Adduction
doThisNotThat: Stand tall and pull the leg across the body slowly; no swinging.
steps: Cuff on the inside ankle, low pulley.
Stand side-on.
Pull the leg across in front of the standing leg.
Return slowly.
cues: Sweep your foot across the floor.
homeSwap: Copenhagen plank on a couch.
note: Adductor strength helps every lateral push-off in basketball and every shot in wrestling.

name: Landmine Squat
doThisNotThat: Hold the bar end at your chest and lean into it slightly; the arc lets you sit deep and upright.
steps: Bar end in a landmine or corner, hold it at your sternum with both hands.
Feet shoulder width, slightly in front of you.
Sit down 3 s to full depth.
Stand driving the bar up the arc.
cues: Push the floor away.
Chest tall to the bar.
homeSwap: Goblet squat with your heaviest DB, 3 s lowering + 1 s pause in the hole, or a 1.5-rep squat (down, half up, down, up).
note: The angled load is forgiving on stiff ankles and hips, so it is a good stepping stone to a full back squat.

name: Overhead Squat
doThisNotThat: Start with a broomstick. Your mobility, not your strength, sets the load here.
steps: Wide snatch grip, bar locked overhead.
Push the bar up and slightly back, armpits forward.
Squat down 3 s keeping the bar over mid-foot.
Stand tall.
cues: Push the bar to the ceiling.
Knees out.
homeSwap: Overhead squat with a broomstick or one light DB held overhead (single-arm).
note: A full-body mobility test for your all-over stiffness: film it monthly; deeper and more upright = progress.

name: Dumbbell Sumo Squat
doThisNotThat: Stand on two boxes or plates so the DB can drop below your feet; more depth = more adductor stretch.
steps: Wide stance, toes out 30-45°.
One DB hanging between your legs by the top head.
Sit straight down 3 s, knees out over the toes.
Stand up squeezing the glutes.
cues: Push your knees out to the walls.
homeSwap: Already home: stand on two stairs or books.
note: Loads your stiff adductors in a long position, which helps squat depth and lateral range.

name: Kettlebell Deadlift
doThisNotThat: Bell between the feet in line with your ankles; hips back and push the floor away.
steps: Bell between your feet, mid-foot line.
Hinge and grip with a flat back.
Push the floor away, stand tall.
Hinge back down with control.
cues: Push the floor away.
Stand tall.
homeSwap: Single-leg DB RDL, 3 s lowering, both DBs in the opposite hand to the working leg.
note: The cleanest way to learn the hinge before a barbell; perfect for home with one heavy DB.

name: Smith Machine Split Squat
doThisNotThat: The bar balances for you, so push close to failure and go deep.
steps: Bar on traps, front foot slightly ahead of the bar line.
Back foot on a bench or floor.
Lower 3 s.
Drive up.
cues: Push the front foot through the floor.
homeSwap: Rear-foot-elevated split squat on a couch or step, DBs at your sides, 3 s lowering.
note: Removes balance so you can load single-leg hard; mix with free versions for athletic transfer.

name: Landmine Reverse Lunge
doThisNotThat: Hold the bar end in the hand opposite the working leg; it challenges hip stability like a punch from a split stance.
steps: Bar end held at the shoulder or hip.
Step back into a lunge.
Lower 2-3 s.
Drive back up through the front foot.
cues: Push the front foot through the floor.
homeSwap: DB reverse lunge with the DB in the opposite hand.
note: Offset load builds the anti-rotation core you need to stay stable while throwing punches from a staggered stance.

name: Step-Down
doThisNotThat: Lower the free heel to the floor in 3 s with the knee over the second toe; do not drop.
steps: Stand on a step on one leg.
Slowly lower the free heel toward the floor.
Tap lightly, stand back up.
cues: Tap the floor like it is hot.
Knee over the little toe.
homeSwap: Already home: a stair.
note: Controlled knee bend on one leg is exactly the landing skill that protects your knees in jumps and cuts.

name: Poliquin Step-Up
doThisNotThat: Heel on a raised plate, knee drives forward over the toes and you push up through the front of the foot. Small range, high quality.
steps: Stand on a low step with the working heel raised on a small plate.
Lower the other heel toward the floor, knee forward.
Push back up through the forefoot.
cues: Push your knee over your toes.
homeSwap: Already home: a book under the heel on a stair.
note: Knee-forward strength for the VMO, a classic knee-health drill for jumping athletes.

name: Hip Airplane
doThisNotThat: Rotate the hip open and closed while keeping the standing foot arched. Hold a wall at first.
steps: Stand on one leg, hinge until your torso is near parallel.
Rotate your pelvis open toward the ceiling slowly.
Rotate back closed.
Keep the standing knee over the toes.
cues: Turn your belly button to the wall.
Grip the floor with your foot.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Trains the hip rotation control your flat-foot cascade throws off; great before cutting sports.

name: Kas Glute Bridge
doThisNotThat: Only move the top third of a hip thrust, keeping chin tucked and ribs down. Constant glute tension.
steps: Hip thrust setup.
Lift to full extension.
Lower only a few inches, then thrust back up.
cues: Drive the bar to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Single-leg hip thrust with shoulders on the couch, DB on the hip, 2 s squeeze at the top.
note: Short range at the top where glutes are shortest: good pump finisher after a full-range hinge.

name: Kneeling Leg Curl
doThisNotThat: Keep the hip still and lower slowly; the hip-flexed position gives more hamstring stretch than lying.
steps: Kneel on the pad, forearms supported.
Working ankle under the roller.
Curl, lower 3 s.
cues: Pull your heel to your butt.
homeSwap: Sliding hamstring curl on socks/towel on a hard floor (hips up), or Nordic curl with feet hooked under a couch.
note: Hip flexion lengthens the hamstrings, which should load them harder at the start of the rep (mechanism-based).

name: Bodyweight Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Go off a stair for the full stretch, pause at the bottom.
steps: Balls of feet on a stair, hold the rail.
Lower 2 s, pause 2 s.
Rise high, squeeze 1 s.
cues: Push the stair down with your big toes.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Once 25 reps is easy, go single-leg: your flat feet benefit most from the single-leg version.

name: Smith Machine Calf Raise
doThisNotThat: Stand on a plate or step for the deep stretch, pause at the bottom.
steps: Bar on traps, balls of feet on a step.
Lower 2 s, pause.
Rise high.
cues: Push the step down with your big toes.
homeSwap: Single-leg calf raise off a stair, holding a DB, 2 s pause at the bottom stretch.
note: Finish each set with bottom-half lengthened partials (Kassiano 2023).

name: Single-Leg Hip Hinge Bodyweight
doThisNotThat: Reach both hands to the floor slowly with hips square; balance is the training.
steps: Stand on one leg, soft knee.
Hinge forward as the back leg rises.
Reach toward the floor 3 s.
Return tall.
cues: Reach your back heel to the wall.
homeSwap: Already home.
note: Daily balance and foot drill: do it barefoot to train the tripod foot.

name: Dumbbell Step-Up to Knee Drive
doThisNotThat: Drive up and snap the opposite knee to hip height, like a sprint stride.
steps: Foot on a knee-height box.
Push through the top foot.
Drive the other knee up fast at the top.
Lower 3 s.
cues: Punch your knee to the ceiling.
homeSwap: Already home: stair step-up with knee drive.
note: Matches the sprint and jump pattern: hip extension on one side, knee drive on the other.
